rounds.text: Menon Bearings Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, underscored by a 28% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 61% surge in profit growth over the same period [E9, E11]. This top-and-bottom-line acceleration is supported by high capital efficiency, with a robust ROCE of 25.5% and an ROE of 22.3% [E6, E7]. Furthermore, institutional money flow is signaling positive accumulation with a holding change of +0.30 percentage points, while the stock maintains a strong technical posture above its moving averages alongside a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E32, E38, E39]. Management is aggressively scaling operations, targeting a 25% year-on-year revenue growth rate for the next few years and an ambitious top-line goal of INR 500 crores by 2028, backed by expanding capacities in the bi-metal and Alkop segments funded entirely through internal accruals [E70, E71, E79, E86, E87]. Conceded: the DCF model points to an intrinsic value below the current market price and the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 7.16x [E2, E33].

The current valuation prices in perfection, leaving a staggering downside risk if growth normalises. A discounted cash flow model explicitly values the stock at Rs 124 per share against its market price of Rs 237, resulting in an extreme margin of safety of -91.1% [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price demands an aggressive 13.9% earnings growth, vastly outstripping the 5.0% assumed in the base case [E35]. This aggressive pricing is compounded by a lofty price-to-book ratio of 7.16x and a P/E multiple of 30.3 [E1, E2]. Conceded: the business maintains strong returns on capital with an ROCE of 25.5% and an ROE of 22.3% [E6, E7]. However, operational headwinds including volatile operating margins, climbing borrowings up to Rs 47 Cr, and stagnant promoter holdings point to an underlying fragility that fails to justify such an inflated multiple [E20, E21, E27, E29].

Conceded: a discounted cash flow calculates intrinsic value at Rs 124 against a market price of Rs 237 [E33], and price-to-book sits at 7.16x [E2]. However, the bear's fixation on static models ignores explosive operational acceleration: trailing twelve-month profit growth surged 61% [E11], completely dwarfing the bear's assumed 5.0% base case [E35], while quarterly net profit jumped 75% year-on-year [E53]. Furthermore, the bear's concern over rising borrowings to Rs 47 Cr [E27] completely misses that capital expenditure is already complete with CWIP dropping 100% to Rs 0 Cr [E28], meaning new capacity is coming online to fund management's targeted 25% year-on-year revenue growth [E86]. Conceded: operating margins read inconsistent over the last two years [E20], but recent quarterly margins expanded to 22% in June 2026—a 3 percentage point year-on-year gain [E19]—alongside a robust pipeline of 51 new parts worth nearly Rs 30 crores [E77] and a sector tailwind score of +0.53 [E58].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 61% [E11] and quarterly net profit surged 75% year-on-year [E53]. However, the bull's reliance on these exceptional growth rates overlooks that the stock's current price of Rs 237 already prices in an aggressive 13.9% earnings growth, vastly outstripping the fundamental base case of 5.0% [E35]. Conceded: CWIP stands at Rs 0 Cr [E28], but borrowings actually rose to Rs 47 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 43 Cr a year earlier [E27], demonstrating that capital needs and debt are climbing despite completed projects. Conceded: June 2026 quarterly operating margins expanded by 3 percentage points [E19], but the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are officially classified as inconsistent over the last two years and two quarters [E20, E21]. Furthermore, cash conversion remains weak with operating cash flow making up only 36% of operating profit in March 2026 [E25], meaning surging profits are failing to convert fully into cash. Finally, promoter holdings have declined to 68.44% in June 2026 from 70.18% in September 2023 [E29], and foreign institutional holdings dropped to 0.14% [E30], contradicting the notion of unreserved institutional conviction.

Conceded: today's price already implies a 13.9% earnings growth against a base case of 5.0% [E35], but this is justified by management's explicit commitment to target a 25% year-on-year revenue growth rate for the next few years and reach INR 500 crores by 2028 [E86, E87]. Conceded: borrowings ticked up to Rs 47 Cr [E27], but the balance sheet remains conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity of 0.25x while all upcoming capacity expansions in bi-metal and Alkop are funded entirely through internal accruals without fresh loans [E26, E79]. Conceded: annual and quarterly operating margins are flagged as inconsistent [E20, E21], yet quarterly operating margins expanded significantly by 3 percentage points year-on-year to reach 22% in June 2026 [E19]. Conceded: cash flow from operations was 36% of operating profit in March 2026 [E25], but the company still generated positive free cash flow of Rs 5 Cr alongside Rs 23 Cr in operating cash flow [E23, E24]. Finally, promoter selling is minor with holdings still robust at 68.44% [E29], and institutional money flow actually reads positive with domestic institutions increasing their stake [E31, E32].

Conceded: management targets 25% year-on-year revenue growth and INR 500 crores by 2028 [E86, E87]. However, relying on ambitious forward targets ignores the fundamental valuation disconnect, where a discounted cash flow model values the stock at just Rs 124 against a market price of Rs 237, resulting in a severe -91.1% margin of safety [E33, E34]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a modest 0.25x and internal accruals fund expansion [E26, E79], but total borrowings still ticked up from Rs 43 Cr to Rs 47 Cr [E27]. Conceded: operating margins reached 22% in June 2026 [E19], but both the yearly and quarterly margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E20, E21], and input costs face fierce headwinds like a 300% surge in carbide tool prices [E75]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 23 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 5 Cr [E23, E24], yet cash conversion remains weak with operating cash flow representing only 36% of operating profit [E25]. Finally, while domestic institutions added a fraction of a percentage point [E31], promoter holdings have steadily declined from 70.18% to 68.44% [E29] while foreign institutional holding has collapsed down to a negligible 0.14% [E30].

evidence.fact: For the Alkop segment, management targets revenue of INR100 crores for the current year and around INR125 crores for next year.
evidence.quote: For this year, we are targeting Alkop for INR100 crores, next year around INR125 crores.

evidence.fact: Management expects export contribution to total revenue to go up to 37% by next year.
evidence.quote: As we expect that by next year, the export may go up to 37% after total revenue.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the underlying demand outlook for the automotive and engineering sector remains encouraging.
evidence.quote: While the global business environment continues to present certain uncertainties, the underlying demand outlook for the automotive and engineering sector remains encouraging.

evidence.fact: Management noted that visits to Canada and USA are expected to yield substantial volumes in the coming period of the year.
evidence.quote: That is because, more particularly, due to our last month's visit to Canada and USA, is expected to yield substantial volumes in the coming period of the year.

evidence.fact: The company continues to operate within its primary segment of auto components where it is seeing sustained demand.
evidence.quote: We continue to operate within our primary segment of auto components where we are seeing sustained demand.

evidence.fact: The company is investing about INR9 crores to INR10 crores this financial year for increasing bi-metal capacity.
evidence.quote: If you go through the presentation, Rucheeta, you will come to know that we are investing about INR9 crores to INR10 crores of rupees for this year, this financial year for increasing the capacity and which is expected to increase the capacity by almost 25% to 30%, which may yield the total revenue of more than INR25 crores, which can generate revenue of INR25 crores.

evidence.fact: The company planned a CapEx of around INR4 crores for the Alkop segment alone for the year.
evidence.quote: And we are having the CapEx of around INR4 crores of for this year in Alkop alone.

evidence.fact: Menon Brakes dynamometer is expected to be commissioned by the end of August.
evidence.quote: And just to give a more deeper explanation, by next month, August end, the machine is supposed to be commissioned at our end.

evidence.fact: Standalone bi-metal sales increased year-on-year by 40.41% and EBITDA increased by approximately 60%.
evidence.quote: Bi-metal Menon Bearings, during the quarter sales increased to INR67.06 crores from INR47.76 crores as compared to the corresponding quarter of the last year that is year-on-year increase of 40.41% and further increased by about 41%. EBITDA is up by ~60%.

evidence.fact: Brakes segment EBITDA margin reached 25% during the quarter.
evidence.quote: But at the same time, I would like to tell you that right from 12% EBITDA earlier, now we have reached to 25% EBITDA in brakes also.And that is above all other segments.

evidence.fact: Prices of consumables such as carbide tools increased by 300%.
evidence.quote: Consumables, for example, carbide tools for all manufacturers, all automobile carbide tools are required.Those carbide tools price are increased by 300%.

evidence.fact: Bi-metal division capacity utilization is at 85%.
evidence.quote: So currently our utilization is at 85%.

evidence.fact: The new development parts pipeline includes 51 new parts across major customers representing a business value of almost INR 30 crores within this year and next year.
evidence.quote: Our new development parts pipeline is robust with 51 new parts across major customers like John Deere for India domestic and exports as well. Eaton, Taco Prestolite and Mayekawa representing a business value of almost INR 30 crores within this year and next year.

evidence.fact: In the Bi-Metal division, the robust pipeline is more than INR 50 crores.
evidence.quote: With this, apart from this, in Bi-Metal division also, we are having a robust pipeline of more than INR 50 crores.

evidence.fact: CapEx for bi-metal and Alkop will be funded through internal accruals only without fresh loans.
evidence.quote: You see, so far as whatever we are considering so far as bi-metal and Alkop is concerned, it will be through internal accruals only, no fresh loan will be taken.

evidence.fact: The Board declared a dividend of Rs 2 per share having face value of Re 1 each.
evidence.quote: Note: The Board has declared Dividend of Rs. 2 per share having face value of Re. 1 each

evidence.fact: Most of the capex that the company is going to do will be financed with internal accruals.
evidence.quote: and whatever capex is that we are going to do that most of it will be financed with internal accruals.

evidence.fact: Merchant export orders were stuck due to backlogs caused by the Strait of Hormuz and war.
evidence.quote: But last three months, those merchant export orders were stuck because of backlog because of the Straight of Hormuz and the war.

evidence.fact: The new labour code was introduced by the government and regulations were issued in April '25.
evidence.quote: Now, as a legal compliance, so the new labour code has been introduced by the government and the regulations have been issued in the month of April '25.

evidence.fact: Export shipments to African countries through Dubai were halted for three months, affecting business to the extent of almost INR 2 crores.
evidence.quote: So what has happened so far as Dubai is concerned, they export to African countries through Dubai. For last three months, we have -- that export is halted. That has affected to the extent of almost INR2 crores of business that we have lost during last three months.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): Management targets Alkop revenue to reach INR100 crores for the current year and around INR125 crores for next year.
evidence.quote: For this year, we are targeting Alkop for INR100 crores, next year around INR125 crores.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next few years): Management committed to target a year-on-year revenue growth rate of 25% for the next few years.
evidence.quote: And again, we will be sustaining this because of increase in the overall turnover which we are targeting at a rate of 25% year-on-year for next few years.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY28): Management committed to take all-out efforts to reach INR 500 crores by 2028.
evidence.quote: And we will take all-out efforts to see how we can reach INR500 crores by '28.
